# VEO 3.1 (Google Flow) — reference for AI video-prompt generation (A.P.G)

> Injected when Target = Veo. Veo is single-shot per generation; for multi-shot use
> TIMESTAMP PROMPTING inside one 8s clip (up to 4 beats). Output as flowing prose.

## Core specs
- Durations: 4s / 6s / 8s (pick deliberately). Use the user's Timing (round to 4/6/8; >8s => timestamp 8s or note Scene Extension).
- Resolution 720p/1080p; aspect 16:9 or 9:16.
- Native synchronized audio, prompt-driven (no knob).

## 5-part formula (flowing prose, NOT labeled fields)
[Cinematography] + [Subject] + [Action] + [Context] + [Style & Ambiance]
- Cinematography: shot type, camera movement, lens, focus, angle.
- Subject: who/what, physical details, wardrobe, age, expression.
- Action: what they do, verbs anchored in time.
- Context: location, time of day, weather, props.
- Style & Ambiance: film stock, era, mood, lighting quality, color palette.

## Audio (Veo's strength) — place each cue INLINE next to its action, never stacked at the end
- Dialogue: `A woman says: "..."` (~2s per line). Add `(no subtitles)` unless captions wanted.
- SFX: anchor to a visible action, be specific.
- Ambient: concrete soundscape.
- Music: specify role + level ("swelling score, ducked under dialogue").

## Negative prompts (Veo supports them) — phrase as positive absence
- Good: "a desolate landscape with no buildings or roads". Bad: "no buildings, no roads".

## Multi-shot = timestamp prompting (DEFAULT unless user wants a single shot)
4 beats x 2s = 8s. Force real cuts:
1. Minimal preamble (<60 words): only invariants (decor, costumes, tone, negatives). Don't describe the opening scene there.
2. Prefix each beat with `Cut to:`.
3. Radically incompatible framings between consecutive beats (wide eye-level -> worm's-eye Dutch; wide -> extreme macro; ground -> top-down; front -> reverse).
4. Discrete self-contained action per beat (not one continuous move).
5. Audio cuts sharply between beats (each beat its own soundscape).
```
[invariants preamble <60 words]
Cut to: [00:00-00:02] [framing], [subject], [action]. [audio].
Cut to: [00:02-00:04] [radically different framing], [action]. [audio].
Cut to: [00:04-00:06] ...
Cut to: [00:06-00:08] ...
```
Single shot only when explicitly requested or the brief is one sustained moment.

## Modes
- Text-to-Video (5-part formula). Frames-to-Video (describe the transition between first/last frame). Ingredients-to-Video (reference up to ~3 images explicitly: "Using the provided images for [X], [Y]..."). Scene Extension (continue from last second).

## Avoid
- Fabrication words (latex/foam/CGI/VFX) — describe the visible on-screen result.
- Stacking audio at the end. Vague ambience. Over-stuffed single shots (>80 words => use timestamps).
- "Cut to" outside timestamp mode. Negative phrasing. Burned-in subtitles by default.

## Style modes mapping (Action/Weird/Beauty sliders)
- ACTION -> timestamp multishot, dynamic movements (tracking, crane, handheld, whip pan), low/Dutch angles, sharp audio cuts.
- WEIRD -> surreal/uncanny: chiaroscuro/low-key, impossible framings, droning specific ambience, dreamlike beats.
- BEAUTY -> auteur/product: 6–8s sustained or elegant beats, golden/soft light, shallow DoF, slow push/dolly, rim light, refined color palette.
Weight by sliders.
